narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Filing Desk"**

Rebuttal looks like a clerk's desk where cases are decided on paper: cool off-white sheets, blue-black ink, thin rule lines between records, and a rubber stamp for the verdict. It is a filing desk, not a dashboard. Nothing glows, floats or gradients. Authority comes from the deterministic decision, so the one loud thing on any page is the firewall's stamp, and everything around it is quiet, typeset record.

Density is that of a well-kept file: generous reading measure (about 42rem for prose), a single centred column (64rem on the home page, 56rem on inner pages), records separated by hairline rules rather than boxed into cards. Pages are walked in order. A route bar across the top says which of the three doors you are at, and a heavy ink rule closes each page with one Next button.

The system has light and dark modes driven by `prefers-color-scheme`. Every colour is a CSS custom property on `:root` in `src/app/globals.css` and is remapped for dark; the frontmatter records the light values, and the sidecar carries the dark ones.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper, blue-black ink, hairline rules; flat, no shadows.
Three stamp inks (allow green, deny red, hold amber) are the only saturated colours, and each always means a verdict or a status.
One action blue for buttons, links and focus.
Public Sans for everything people read; IBM Plex Mono only for identifiers.
Tabular figures everywhere, so money and counts line up.
Every page ends with one Next step.

rules.name: The Stamp Ink Rule
rules.body: Allow green, deny red and hold amber are the only saturated colours, and they always carry their meaning (allowed, denied, held or caution). A chart, illustration or decoration never uses red or green for anything else.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Action blue means "you can click this" and nothing else.

rules.name: The Faint Floor Rule
rules.body: Faint holds WCAG AA on paper (4.58:1 light, 5.4:1 dark). It is for text on paper only; on sunk paper it drops to 4.25:1, so text on sunk uses graphite or ink.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Identifiers Rule
rules.body: Plex Mono is reserved for identifiers: ids, hashes, source citations, model names and file paths. Prose, labels, numbers and headings stay in Public Sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: The body sets `tnum` on, so every amount, score and count lines up in columns. Large proof figures also use tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Walk In Order Rule
rules.body: Every route page carries the route bar (three numbered doors; the current one in ink with a filled ink disc, earlier ones graphite, later ones faint) and ends with one Next step: a 2px ink rule, a sentence, and one primary button to the next door.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: One primary (action blue) button per section. Any other action in that section is a quiet button or a text link.

rules.name: The Paper Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If a surface needs separating, give it a rule line or sunk paper, never a shadow.

dos: **Do** keep allow green, deny red and hold amber for their meanings (allowed, denied, held or caution), and use them nowhere else.
**Do** compute every figure on a page from committed data (the eval report, the recorded run, the ledger) and label anything synthetic, simulated or replayed in plain words next to it.
**Do** date proof figures and name their model and run count in a label line beneath them.
**Do** set identifiers in IBM Plex Mono and everything else in Public Sans.
**Do** give each section one primary button; extra actions are quiet buttons or links.
**Do** end every route page with the Next step, and open it with the route bar.
**Do** separate records with rule lines and sunk paper.
**Do** check new text colours for AA against the surface they sit on; faint is cleared on paper only.
donts: **Don't** use red or green in a chart, illustration or decoration for anything other than denied or allowed.
**Don't** add drop shadows, glows or gradients.
**Don't** use PayPal's logos, brand colours or anything that imitates its checkout button. "PayPal" appears only as plain text.
**Don't** use mono for prose, labels or headings to make them look technical.
**Don't** animate the stamp after it lands, or animate it at all when reduced motion is requested.
**Don't** show a number that is not read from committed data, or a synthetic case without its label.
